# Generated code

C++ code generated by `snmpwrap-mibgen` from the MIB files in [../mibs](../mibs).

| Folder | MIB | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| [snmpwrapper_demo_mib/](snmpwrapper_demo_mib) | [SNMPWRAPPER-DEMO-MIB](../mibs/SNMPWRAPPER-DEMO-MIB.txt) | `examples/mib_agent.cpp`, `examples/mib_client.cpp` |
| [snmpwrapper_test_mib/](snmpwrapper_test_mib) | [SNMPWRAPPER-TEST-MIB](../mibs/SNMPWRAPPER-TEST-MIB.txt) | `test/agents/generated_test_agent.cpp`, `test/agents/generated_client_check.cpp` |

**Do not edit these files.** The build regenerates them whenever the MIB (or the generator)
changes; they are written here instead of the build directory only so you can read and review
them. Each folder is built as a static library of the same name (see [CMakeLists.txt](CMakeLists.txt)):

```cmake
target_link_libraries(my_agent PRIVATE snmpwrapper_demo_mib)   # adds the include path and snmpwrap
```

What to look at in `<name>.hpp`:

* `namespace oids` – the OID of every MIB node,
* `enum class …` – named numbers (`INTEGER { … }`, TruthValue, …),
* `struct …Index` / `struct …Entry` / `struct …Values` – table index, row, values for row creation,
* `class Instrumentation` – the interface an agent implements (one method per MIB object),
* `registerMib()`, `bind()`, `send…()` – registration and notifications,
* `class Client` – typed client access.

To regenerate by hand (e.g. for a MIB of your own):

```sh
snmpwrap-mibgen --module SNMPWRAPPER-DEMO-MIB --out generated/snmpwrapper_demo_mib mibs/SNMPWRAPPER-DEMO-MIB.txt
```

The files are only rewritten when their content changes. `ninja clean` / `make clean` removes them;
the next build creates them again.
